Regarding the effectiveness of the described physical therapy techniques:

Myofascial release (MFR) is generally considered effective for treating myofascial pain syndrome and related musculoskeletal issues. By applying gentle, sustained pressure to the fascia, MFR aims to release restrictions in the connective tissue, which can help alleviate pain, reduce muscle tension, and improve range of motion. Clinical evidence and patient reports often support its use as a complementary therapy for chronic pain conditions, though individual results may vary based on the severity of the condition and the skill of the practitioner. It is most effective when integrated into a broader treatment plan that may include exercise, stretching, and other modalities.
